facts.title: Experience League: Brand Concierge overview
facts.quote: Brand Concierge is an agentic platform that enables businesses and brands to launch personalized conversational experiences on their customer-facing surfaces: websites, mobile apps, and other digital properties.
facts.supports: Adobe's own definition of Brand Concierge: an agentic platform for conversational experiences on a brand's websites, mobile apps and other digital properties.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Brand Concierge
facts.quote: It draws on approved brand content, product catalogs, and other trusted sources, ensuring that all information is brand-safe and up-to-date.
facts.supports: Adobe says Brand Concierge draws on approved brand content, product catalogs and other trusted sources.

facts.title: Experience League: Manage a concierge
facts.quote: Answers general brand questions, including FAQs, policies, pricing, how-to guidance, and support topics
facts.supports: The Site Advisory skill, active by default, is the one that answers general questions such as FAQs, policies and pricing.

facts.title: Experience League: Create and manage knowledge sources for Brand Concierge
facts.quote: A knowledge source is the content that a concierge can use when answering visitor questions. Every concierge requires at least one configured knowledge source.
facts.supports: A knowledge source is the content a concierge answers from, and each concierge needs at least one.

facts.title: Experience League: Create and manage knowledge sources for Brand Concierge
facts.quote: Crawls a sitemap, selected individual URLs, or URLs supplied in a CSV file.
facts.supports: With a Website Links knowledge source the brand chooses what is crawled: a sitemap, individual URLs, or a CSV list of URLs.

facts.title: Experience League: Create and manage knowledge sources for Brand Concierge
facts.quote: This native integration makes updated AEM Sites content available to Brand Concierge automatically. A separate crawl or refresh step is not required.
facts.supports: An AEM Sites knowledge source (Content AI index) passes updated AEM Sites content to Brand Concierge without a separate crawl or refresh.

facts.title: Experience League: Create and manage knowledge sources for Brand Concierge
facts.quote: Schedule a refresh frequency, such as weekly on a specified day and time, to keep the knowledge source current as the website changes.
facts.supports: A Website Links knowledge source can be refreshed on a schedule, for example weekly, to stay current.

facts.title: Experience League: Current release information
facts.quote: In addition, Brand Concierge now supports PDF/DOCX file upload.
facts.supports: The February 2026 release notes say Brand Concierge supports PDF and DOCX file upload for knowledge sources.

facts.title: Experience League: Preparing your content and visitor journey
facts.quote: The three types of knowledge sources: website URLs, PDFs, and product spreadsheets
facts.supports: Adobe's go-live guide names three types of knowledge sources: website URLs, PDFs and product spreadsheets.

facts.title: Experience League: Create and manage knowledge sources for Brand Concierge
facts.quote: A concierge answers questions using only its configured knowledge sources. It does not answer from general world knowledge.
facts.supports: The concierge answers only from its configured knowledge sources, not from general world knowledge.

facts.title: Experience League: Create and manage knowledge sources for Brand Concierge
facts.quote: If a visitor asks about information outside the configured knowledge sources, the concierge is designed to indicate that it does not have the information instead of generating an unsupported answer.
facts.supports: When a question falls outside the knowledge sources, the concierge is designed to say it does not have the information.

facts.title: Experience League: Frequently asked questions
facts.quote: Options include displaying a graceful “I can’t help with that” message, suggesting alternative questions, linking to self-service resources, or automatically escalating the inquiry to a human agent.
facts.supports: The brand configures the fallback when the concierge cannot answer: a decline message, alternative questions, self-service links, or escalation to a person.

facts.title: Experience League: Brand Concierge overview
facts.quote: Every conversation is grounded in the brand’s own content and guardrails, and integrations let insights from those conversations flow into the rest of the brand’s ecosystem, such as Marketo Engage.
facts.supports: Adobe states every conversation is grounded in the brand's own content and guardrails.

facts.title: Experience League: Manage a concierge
facts.quote: Whether and how source references appear in a response
facts.supports: A Citations chat component controls whether and how source references are shown in a response.

facts.title: Experience League: Manage a concierge
facts.quote: For example, guardrails can exclude legal topics, compliance topics, or competitor discussions, while suggestions can provide follow-up prompt ideas.
facts.supports: Guardrails can exclude legal topics, compliance topics or competitor discussions, and the brand reviews and edits them.

facts.title: Experience League: Frequently asked questions
facts.quote: Safety guardrails, along with content and profanity filters, are enforced at the system level regardless of your own configuration. Anything specific to your brand or industry can be layered on top through the instructions you configure.
facts.supports: System-level safety guardrails and content filters always apply, and brand or industry rules are layered on top through instructions.

facts.title: Experience League: Go-live checklist for a concierge
facts.quote: Review the concierge instructions and guardrails against applicable brand guidelines.
facts.supports: Adobe's go-live checklist has the brand review and approve the instructions and guardrails before launch.

facts.title: Experience League: Brand Concierge help
facts.quote: To provide a transparent and trustworthy experience, Adobe Brand Concierge users are responsible for adding a short disclosure within their conversation experience.
facts.supports: The brand is responsible for adding a conversational AI disclosure in the conversation experience.

facts.title: Experience League: Frequently asked questions
facts.quote: You can control your brand voice directly in the UI by configuring elements such as tone (ranging from formal to casual), language (from simple to technical), and personality (for example, helpful, enthusiastic, or professional).
facts.supports: Brand voice is configured in the UI through tone, language and personality settings.

facts.title: Experience League: Brand Concierge help
facts.quote: Brand expression is set using attributes such as formality, warmth, playfulness, and energy, rather than a single named style.
facts.supports: Brand expression is set with attributes such as formality, warmth, playfulness and energy.

facts.title: Experience League: Evaluate a concierge
facts.quote: Evaluations help you build confidence that a concierge’s responses are accurate before the concierge is reviewed by anyone outside your immediate team.
facts.supports: Evaluations are Adobe's repeatable way to check answer accuracy before wider review.

facts.title: Experience League: Measuring quality and setting guardrails
facts.quote: What a golden set is: real visitor questions paired with ideal answers
facts.supports: Adobe's go-live guide defines the golden set as real visitor questions paired with ideal answers.

facts.title: Experience League: Evaluate a concierge
facts.quote: Checks how the concierge handles questions it should not answer but that are not harmful, such as questions about a competitor or an unrelated topic.
facts.supports: An out-of-scope evaluation type tests how the concierge handles questions it should not answer.

facts.title: Experience League: Go-live checklist for a concierge
facts.quote: Establish a recurring process for reviewing conversation transcripts and adding new evaluation questions as they surface.
facts.supports: Adobe's checklist calls for a recurring review of transcripts and new evaluation questions after launch.

facts.title: Experience League: Live chat and meeting booking overview
facts.quote: Live chat and meeting booking are the two ways Brand Concierge hands that conversation to a human without losing the context the visitor already provided.
facts.supports: Handoff to a person is by live chat or meeting booking, with the conversation context carried over.

facts.title: Experience League: Manage a concierge
facts.quote: These capabilities are powered by a companion product called Adobe Marketo Qualifier, and are offered to visitors through the Handoff to sales skill.
facts.supports: Live chat and meeting booking are powered by a separate companion product, Adobe Marketo Qualifier, through the Handoff to sales skill.

facts.title: Experience League: Live chat and meeting booking overview
facts.quote: both route through Adobe Marketo Qualifier (formerly Sales Qualifier), where your representatives connect their calendars, set their availability, and take chats.
facts.supports: Adobe Marketo Qualifier is the product formerly named Sales Qualifier, and it is where representatives take chats and set availability.

facts.title: Experience League: Frequently asked questions
facts.quote: In the current scope, Concierge is focused on anonymous visitors: it answers from the conversation and your knowledge base (website and catalog), not from a live lookup of identity or journey state in Real-Time CDP.
facts.supports: Adobe's FAQ says the current scope is anonymous visitors, with no live lookup of identity in Real-Time CDP.

facts.title: Experience League: Current release information
facts.quote: Brand Concierge Integration with Real-Time CDP (Limited Availability)
facts.supports: The April 2026 release notes label the Real-Time CDP integration Limited Availability.

facts.title: Experience League: Current release information
facts.quote: Enhance the quality and relevance of conversational responses by incorporating Real-Time CDP context, such as user attributes, behavioral signals, and prior interactions to better align replies with user intent.
facts.supports: What the Limited Availability Real-Time CDP integration does: brings user attributes, behavioral signals and prior interactions into responses.

facts.title: Experience League: Frequently asked questions
facts.quote: Brand Concierge can be used across a wide range of industries, including retail and e-commerce, travel and hospitality, financial services, healthcare (with compliance controls), media and entertainment, and technology and software.
facts.supports: Adobe's FAQ lists financial services among the industries that can use Brand Concierge.

facts.title: Experience League: Financial Services Use Cases
facts.quote: the agent must guide customers toward suitable products based on stated needs without constituting investment advice, and prohibited topics (specific return projections, guarantees, comparative performance claims) must be explicitly defined and enforced.
facts.supports: Adobe's financial services blueprint says guardrails must keep the agent short of investment advice and define prohibited topics, with compliance and legal review.

facts.title: Experience League: Financial Services Use Cases
facts.quote: The content integration layer must be grounded in compliance-approved product descriptions, disclosures, and FAQs rather than dynamically generated claims, ensuring every response the agent delivers has been reviewed by legal and regulatory teams before deployment.
facts.supports: Adobe's financial services blueprint says the content the agent answers from must be compliance-approved descriptions, disclosures and FAQs.

facts.title: Experience League: Financial Services Use Cases
facts.quote: Live agent handoff must be configured for scenarios in which customer needs exceed the scope of the conversational guide
facts.supports: Adobe's financial services blueprint requires live agent handoff when a customer's needs exceed the guide's scope.

facts.title: Experience League: Developer and customization guide
facts.quote: Please do not enter any sensitive personal information (e.g., financial or health data).
facts.supports: The sample privacy notice in Adobe's developer guide asks visitors not to enter sensitive personal information such as financial data.

not_found: claim 2: a content approval or sign-off workflow inside Brand Concierge. The pages only describe the brand choosing which sitemap, URLs, AEM index or catalog to load, and reviewing drafts. Looked in the knowledge sources, manage a concierge, FAQ and go-live checklist pages.

claim 2: steps for uploading documents. PDF and DOCX upload is named only in the February 2026 release notes and the go-live video page; the knowledge sources page (updated Oct 2, 2026) lists three types: AEM Sites (Content AI index), Website Links and Product Catalog.

claim 4: any feature that enforces required legal or compliance wording, or adds a disclaimer to each answer. The pages offer free-text instructions and guardrails, one 'Legal disclaimer text' setting under visual style, and a disclosure the brand must add itself.
claim 6: pass marks or a required number of test questions. The go-live video page lists 'How many question-and-answer pairs to include' as a video topic but the page text gives no number.
claim 7: handoff to a service desk, contact center or any third-party live chat product. Every handoff page describes the Handoff to sales skill, sales representatives and Adobe Marketo Qualifier.

claim 8: any page on signed-in or authenticated visitors, passing an identity to the concierge, or setting up the Real-Time CDP integration. Only the FAQ answer and one April 2026 release note line cover it.

claim 9: no Brand Concierge page covers financial regulation, advice rules, or handling of account or sensitive personal data beyond the FAQ's industry list, the GDPR and CCPA answer and the sample privacy notice. The financial services guidance quoted here is from Adobe's Experience Platform blueprints, not the Brand Concierge product docs. The product description at helpx.adobe.com/legal/product-descriptions/adobe-brand-concierge.html returned 403 from here and was not read.
cautions: Anonymous visitors only today. The FAQ says: 'In the current scope, Concierge is focused on anonymous visitors' and 'Tailoring responses by "does this visitor have a profile?" or "where are they in a journey?" is a future enhancement.' The Real-Time CDP integration is labeled Limited Availability in the April 2026 release notes. So do not say it answers questions about a customer's own accounts or balances. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-concierge/content/documentation/brand-concierge-faq and https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-concierge/content/release-notes/current

Adobe's own pages are not consistent on this. The same FAQ says the AI is 'specifically trained on your organization's content and customer data' and gives 'personalized responses informed by individual customer behavior'; the Brand Concierge help page's Financial services row says it 'provides account information'; and the Experience Platform blueprints describe 'real-time profile lookup'. None of these pages says how, and the FAQ's anonymous-visitor answer is the most specific statement. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-concierge/content/documentation/overview

Handoff runs on a separate product. Live chat and meeting booking 'are powered by a companion product called Adobe Marketo Qualifier' ('formerly Sales Qualifier'), need access to it, and are framed as Handoff to sales with sales representatives; the default triggers are sales intents (pricing, demos, RFPs, trials). The FAQ lists 'automatically escalating the inquiry to a human agent' as a fallback option but no page documents a service or support handoff. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-concierge/content/documentation/sales-handoff/overview

The home page (last updated January 15, 2026) still lists handoff as 'Upcoming feature - Seamless human handoff', while the September 2026 release notes show Live Chat and Meeting Booking as released. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-concierge/content/home
Live chat data: 'Live chat conversations are retained for 30 days.' https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-concierge/content/documentation/sales-handoff/overview

Knowledge source limits: the AEM Sites source applies when 'The customer uses AEM Sites as a Cloud Service with Content AI enabled'; the Product Catalog source is for 'approximately fewer than 100' products or services; documents (PDF, DOCX) are not on the knowledge sources page's list of types. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-concierge/content/documentation/knowledge-sources/knowledge-sources

Guardrail limits: the skills page lists 'add a new guardrail category the framework does not support' under 'Not self-serve, needs engineering'. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-concierge/content/documentation/skills-and-integrations

Sample notices in the developer guide: the sample privacy notice says 'Please do not enter any sensitive personal information (e.g., financial or health data).' and the sample disclaimer says 'AI responses may be inaccurate or misleading. Be sure to double check answers and sources.' Both are sample configuration text a brand can change, but a bank will notice them. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-concierge/content/documentation/developer-customization-guide

The FAQ says 'Adobe consultants handle prompt engineering in the background', while the newer Composer pages describe self-serve setup by a marketer. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-concierge/content/documentation/brand-concierge-faq

Other availability labels: 'Multilingual Concierge Support (Limited Availability)' with validated support for Spanish and French (release notes); 'Brand Concierge for the Web SDK is currently in beta' (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/tags/extensions/client/web-sdk/configure/brand-concierge). The release notes also state 'All features are generally available unless indicated otherwise.'

The three bc.regulated facts from the Financial Services Use Cases page are architecture guidance written as requirements ('must be configured'), on a page that names the Product Advisor Agent and AEP Agent Orchestrator. They say what a bank should set up, not what the product does by default. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/blueprints-learn/architecture/industry-use-cases/financial-services-overview
The go-live guide pages are video pages; quotes from them are the page's summary bullets, not the video narration. The home page quote (bc.what.2) is from a page last updated January 15, 2026.
Quotes were picked to contain no em dashes. Several match as lowercase fragments of a longer sentence (bc.handoff.3, bc.regulated.2); capitalize with care when shown.
